sub_answers.sub_question: How does mirror symmetry breaking from Coulomb displacement and charge-dependent nuclear forces affect ANC-to-width mapping?
sub_answers.text: Coulomb interaction breaks isospin symmetry and modifies mirror mass differences relevant for ANC-to-width relations [d83088s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What errors arise from assuming peripheral dominance and single-particle structure when using ANCs to predict widths?
How does model dependence in ANC extraction (optical potentials, reaction mechanism) contribute to uncertainty?
sub_answers.text: Extraction of isospin-nonconserving matrix elements requires global parameterizations that depend on model choices and short-range correlation treatments [d16198s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Why can ANC-based methods fail for broad resonances or overlapping resonances where single-level approximations break down?
What are the limitations of neglecting channel coupling and continuum contributions when using ANC-derived widths?
sub_answers.text: Charge-dependent forces and Coulomb interaction cause non-negligible isospin mixing that can couple channels and modify observables built from single-channel ANCs [d83088s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are ANC-derived resonance widths used in calculating thermonuclear reaction rates for stellar nucleosynthesis?
sub_answers.text: ANC-derived resonance information is combined with other indirect methods to determine absolute astrophysical reaction rates for key stellar reactions like 13C(α,n)16O [d36408s0p0]. [d36408s0p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: In what ways do ANC constraints aid the analysis of astrophysical proton-capture reactions near the drip line?
sub_answers.text: ANC constraints are used alongside methods such as the Trojan Horse Method to resolve inconsistencies in cross sections for reactions at astrophysical energies near resonances relevant to nucleosynthesis [d36408s0p0]. [d36408s0p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: How do ANC-based predictions influence the interpretation of experimental data for exotic, short-lived nuclei?
sub_answers.text: ANC-based analyses provide accurate absolute values of astrophysical factors for reactions involving short-lived or otherwise hard-to-measure nuclei by using indirect approaches that avoid direct cross section measurements [d36408s0p0]. [d36408s0p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: What advantages do ANC methods offer compared with direct width measurements for narrow resonances?
sub_answers.text: ANC methods allow determination of absolute cross sections and reaction rates without relying on direct, sometimes inconsistent, low-energy measurements by using indirect techniques that can unambiguously fix the absolute value of the astrophysical factor [d36408s0p0]. [d36408s0p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: How have ANC-based predictions been validated against measured resonance widths in well-studied mirror pairs?
What is the formal definition of an asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) in nuclear physics?
sub_answers.text:
The asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) is a parameter used in nuclear physics associated with the amplitude of the tail of a bound-state overlap function in peripheral reactions [d69413s0p0].
The ANC is used as an indirect method to determine absolute reaction cross sections at astrophysical energies when combined with other techniques [d36408s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What is a mirror nucleus and what are the typical symmetry relations between mirror pairs?
sub_answers.text:
Mirror hypernuclei pairs are pairs of nuclei studied together as mirrors, exemplified by pairs such as 10LambdaBe–10LambdaB and 12LambdaB–12LambdaC [d110027s0p0].
Mirror pairs exhibit systematic correlations, for example linear correlations between mirror hypernuclei in Lambda separation energies and in charge radii [d110027s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How is a resonance width defined in terms of decay probability and scattering theory?
sub_answers.text:
A resonance width characterizes a resonant state that is included explicitly in scattering amplitudes and the S matrix in scattering theory [d69413s0p0].
Resonant states and their widths are handled by representing the corresponding parts of the phase shift and fitting parameters in the S matrix to phase shift data [d69413s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What is the theoretical link between ANCs of bound states and widths of mirror resonances?
Which experimental observables are commonly reported as ANCs in nuclear data compilations?
sub_answers.text:
ANC values are commonly reported from alpha-transfer reaction measurements [d69413s0p0].
ANCs are also reported and used in combination with indirect methods such as the Trojan Horse Method to determine astrophysical reaction factors and absolute cross sections [d36408s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What is the single-particle relation between ANC, spectroscopic factor, and single-particle wave function amplitude?
How does the R-matrix formalism express resonance widths in terms of reduced width amplitudes or channel radii?
What role do Coulomb-modified asymptotic forms play in converting proton ANCs to mirror neutron resonance properties?
How are ANCs extracted experimentally via peripheral transfer reactions such as (d,p) or (3He,d)?
sub_answers.text: Peripheral transfer reactions such as deuteron stripping probe the peripheral part of the overlap amplitude and can be used to populate bound and resonance states for extracting asymptotic properties of the wave function [d24171s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What approximations are involved in using single-channel potential models to compute ANCs and widths?
sub_answers.text: Treating the final-state fragment–target potential as real to support bound states and as complex to describe scattering is an inconsistent approximation that produces an auxiliary interior matrix element in reaction calculations [d24171s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In what ways do Coulomb-induced mirror symmetry violations and isospin-breaking, charge-dependent nuclear interactions modify the relationship between a bound-state asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) in one mirror nucleus and the resonant width in its mirror partner? Cite specific mechanisms (Coulomb displacement energies, proton vs neutron separation energies) and quantify typical shifts.
sub_answers.text: Coulomb interaction and isospin-symmetry-breaking (ISB) parts of the nuclear interaction break mirror symmetry and thus modify relations between a bound-state ANC in one mirror nucleus and the resonant width in its mirror partner by shifting energies and mirror displacement energies [d83088s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which systematic biases occur when converting ANCs into particle-decay widths under the assumptions of peripheral reaction dominance and pure single-particle overlaps? Identify sources of error (non-peripheral contributions, configuration mixing, spectroscopic factor quenching) and give typical magnitude ranges reported in the literature.
sub_answers.text: Peripheral-reaction dominance assumptions are central to ANC extractions and dispersion/asymptotic treatments emphasize that peripheral partial amplitudes must be treated with correct three-body Coulomb dynamics to avoid bias in deduced quantities [d57152s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How does the choice of reaction model and inputs used to extract ANCs—such as optical model potentials, transfer-reaction DWBA/FRA approximations, or coupled-channels treatments—propagate into uncertainty on deduced widths? Request concrete comparisons (different global potentials, parameter variations) and reported uncertainty estimates.
sub_answers.text: ANCs extracted with reaction models that combine dispersion theory and conventional DWBA must include the three-body Coulomb dynamics in peripheral partial amplitudes to avoid systematic errors from approximate treatments [d57152s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain the failure modes of ANC-to-width prescriptions for resonances that are broad or lie close to other states: how do energy-dependent level shifts, interference between nearby levels, and breakdown of single-level Breit–Wigner approximations invalidate ANC-based width predictions? Provide examples and quantitative criteria for breakdown.
sub_answers.text: Peripheral ANC-based prescriptions rely on single-level, well-isolated resonances; when levels are broad or closely spaced the single-pole peripheral approximation breaks down because level interference and energy-dependent shifts are not accounted for by simple asymptotic formulas [d57152s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What errors result from ignoring reaction-channel coupling and non-resonant continuum (e.g., virtual excitations, continuum–continuum coupling) when using ANCs to infer resonance widths? Specify which continuum effects (coupled-channels, doorway states, threshold effects) alter the mapping and how large their impact can be.
sub_answers.text: Neglecting three-body Coulomb dynamics, reaction-channel coupling, or non-resonant continuum contributions leads to errors because the peripheral partial amplitudes are altered by Coulomb and continuum coupling and thus the ANC-to-width mapping is changed [d57152s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe concrete methods that convert asymptotic normalization coefficients (ANCs) into partial or total resonance widths for use in computing stellar thermonuclear reaction rates (e.g., via R-matrix or Breit–Wigner formalisms), and list the formulae and input parameters required for rate integrations in networks for H/He burning and explosive scenarios.
sub_answers.text:
Asymptotic normalization coefficients (ANCs) are used to fix reaction-model couplings that enter R-matrix and Breit–Wigner descriptions of resonances by providing the external normalization of bound-state wavefunctions [d28818s0p0][d142355s0p0].
The input quantities required for converting ANCs into partial proton widths include the ANC value, resonance energy, channel radius, reduced mass, and penetration factors for the outgoing particle [d142355s0p0][d28818s0p0].
Those partial widths feed into Breit–Wigner or R-matrix expressions for the resonance contribution to cross sections and into S-factor formulas that are then thermally averaged over a Maxwellian to produce reaction rates for H/He burning and explosive networks [d142355s0p0][d133602s0p0].
Network rate integrations require the resonance energies, total and partial widths (including gamma widths where relevant), the astrophysical S(E) from direct capture or interference terms, and temperature-dependent folding to compute the rate over the relevant Gamow window [d133602s0p0][d142355s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain how experimentally or theoretically determined ANCs constrain proton-capture S-factors and reaction rates for proton-rich isotopes near the proton drip line (for example 17F, 18Ne, 26Si), including how ANC limits reduce uncertainty in low-energy extrapolations and resonance versus direct-capture contributions.
sub_answers.text:
ANCs determined experimentally or theoretically are used to constrain effective-field-theory or model couplings that set the magnitude of low-energy direct-capture S-factors for proton-rich systems near the drip line [d28818s0p0].
Applying ANC constraints in an NLO EFT for a mirror capture case produced an S(0) with substantially reduced uncertainty, giving S(0)=21.3±0.7 eV·b and halving prior recommended uncertainties [d28818s0p0].
Those ANC limits thereby narrow uncertainties in low-energy extrapolations and help separate the relative contributions of direct-capture amplitudes and narrow-resonance components in the total astrophysical rate [d28818s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Detail how ANC-informed theoretical widths are used to interpret measurements of decay branches, resonance energies, and cross sections for short-lived exotic nuclei produced in radioactive-beam experiments (mention techniques such as transfer reactions, Trojan-horse, and invariant-mass spectroscopy), and how ANCs help assign spin-parity and partial widths.
sub_answers.text:
ANC-informed theoretical widths are incorporated as fixed external amplitudes or constraints in R-matrix fits to measured cross sections and decay-branch data for short-lived exotic nuclei [d18533s0p0][d28818s0p0].
R-matrix analyses that include ANC constraints enable consistent extraction of resonance energies and partial widths from combined channels and are used to interpret experimental cross sections in radioactive-beam studies [d18533s0p0].
Using ANCs to set the external capture strength helps in assigning spin-parity and partial widths by comparing the fitted amplitudes and interference patterns against measured decay branches and energy spectra [d18533s0p0][d28818s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List specific practical advantages of using ANC-based determinations of narrow resonance strengths (e.g., reduced dependence on absolute beam-target normalization, ability to infer proton partial widths from peripheral transfer data, and utility when direct resonance scans are impossible), with quantitative examples of uncertainty reduction where available.
sub_answers.text:
ANC-based determinations reduce reliance on absolute beam-target normalization because peripheral transfer data fix the external capture amplitude independently of absolute cross-section scale [d28818s0p0].
ANCs allow proton partial widths to be inferred from peripheral transfer reactions, which is practical when direct resonance scans are experimentally infeasible [d28818s0p0].
Applying ANC constraints in an EFT analysis reduced the S(0) uncertainty by a factor of two in the cited mirror-capture case, demonstrating substantial quantitative uncertainty reduction [d28818s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Summarize case studies comparing ANC-derived widths to directly measured resonance widths in mirror nuclei pairs (for example 13N/13C, 17F/17O, 27P/27Mg), describing the level of agreement, calibrations applied (isospin symmetry corrections), and lessons for extrapolating ANC results to unmeasured proton-rich mirrors.
sub_answers.text:
Mirror-process studies using ANCs, such as relating 7Be(p,γ)8B to the mirror 7Li(n,γ)8Li, have been used to fix EFT couplings and reproduce model results to high precision across the low-energy range [d28818s0p0].
Comparisons of resonance parameters extracted at Breit–Wigner and pole positions show qualitative similarity, which supports calibrations based on isospin symmetry when extrapolating ANC results between mirrors [d18424s0p0].
These comparisons indicate that with appropriate isospin-symmetry corrections ANC-derived widths for proton-rich mirrors can provide accurate estimates useful for extrapolation to unmeasured cases [d28818s0p0][d18424s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide the precise mathematical definition of an asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) used in nuclear physics, including its expression as the amplitude of the tail of a bound-state overlap function (Whittaker or Hankel asymptotic form), normalization conventions, and relation to single-particle wavefunctions and spectroscopic factors.
sub_answers.text: The asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) is the amplitude that quantifies the magnitude of the bound-state overlap function in its asymptotic (large-distance) region and is used to characterize the tail of the bound-state wavefunction for a cluster configuration [d69413s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Define a mirror nucleus pair and describe the structural symmetry relations usually assumed for mirror pairs: isospin/charge symmetry, expected equal spectroscopic factors or overlap functions, typical Coulomb-energy shifts and mirror energy differences, and examples of isobaric analogue states.
sub_answers.text: A mirror nucleus pair consists of two nuclei with their numbers of protons and neutrons interchanged, exemplified by the listed mirror hypernuclei pairs such as 10LambdaBe–10LambdaB and 12LambdaB–12LambdaC [d110027s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Give the rigorous definitions of a resonance width from decay-probability and scattering-theory perspectives: lifetime relation Γ = ħ/τ, partial versus total widths, Breit–Wigner parameterization, S-matrix pole definition, and connection to scattering phase shifts and cross section profiles.
sub_answers.text: Resonant states appear as structures in scattering described by an S matrix and associated phase shifts, and resonances are treated explicitly in scattering amplitudes when constructing the S matrix for elastic scattering [d69413s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain theoretical frameworks that link the ANC of a bound state to the width of its mirror unbound resonance, e.g., analytic continuation of overlap functions, mirror symmetry/charge-exchange arguments, R-matrix or potential-model formulas relating ANC magnitudes to partial widths and the assumptions/approximations involved.
sub_answers.text: Theoretical links between ANCs and mirror unbound resonances are developed in dispersion (asymptotic) theories combined with reaction formalisms, where peripheral transfer amplitudes and their asymptotic behavior are used to relate bound-state ANC information to properties of unbound states accessed in mirror reactions [d57152s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List the experimental quantities and derived parameters that are typically reported as or used to extract ANCs in nuclear data compilations: transfer-reaction differential cross sections ((d,p),(p,d),(3He,d)), extracted ANC values and units, spectroscopic factors, reduced widths, radiative-capture S-factors, reported uncertainties, and which databases/catalogs (EXFOR, ENSDF, NNDC) tabulate them.
sub_answers.text: Experimental extractions of ANCs commonly use peripheral transfer reactions and indirect methods, including alpha-transfer and proton or triton transfer measurements, and the extracted quantities reported include ANC values, spectroscopic information, reduced widths, radiative-capture S-factors, and associated uncertainties that feed into reaction-rate determinations [d69413s0p0][d57152s0p0][d36408s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Derive the quantitative relation in a single-particle framework among the asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC), the spectroscopic factor (or occupancy), and the normalization/amplitude of the single-particle radial wave function at large r; include the convention-dependent factors (e.g., Whittaker/Coulomb functions, matching radius) needed to convert single-particle amplitude to ANC.

In the R‑matrix description of a resonance, how are the observable partial and total widths written in terms of reduced width amplitudes (γ_c) and channel radii a_c? Provide the formulae linking γ_c^2, the penetration/shift functions, level matrix elements, and the boundary-condition dependence needed to get physical Γ values.

When relating mirror states, how do Coulomb-modified asymptotic wave functions (Coulomb wave/Whittaker functions) alter the mapping between a proton ANC and the corresponding neutron resonance parameters (e.g., resonance energy, width, and reduced width)? Specify the role of Sommerfeld parameter, Coulomb barrier effects on external normalization, and any required scaling factors.
sub_answers.text: Coulomb three-body dynamics modify the external (asymptotic) normalization of charged-particle overlaps and thus alter the quantitative mapping between a proton ANC and the corresponding neutron resonance parameters through Coulomb-modified asymptotic behavior of the wave function [d57152s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What experimental observables and reaction-model ingredients are used to extract ANCs from peripheral transfer reactions such as (d,p) and (3He,d)? List the specific measured quantities (differential cross sections at forward angles), necessary reaction calculations (DWBA/ADWA/Faddeev), optical potentials, and the procedures to isolate the peripheral amplitude and deduce the ANC.
sub_answers.text:
Peripheral transfer experiments measure differential cross sections at forward angles to probe the asymptotic tail of the overlap and extract ANCs [d57152s0p0].
Extraction requires reaction-model calculations such as DWBA or other approaches that correctly treat the peripheral amplitude and the three-body Coulomb dynamics of the transfer mechanism [d57152s0p0].
Indirect methods such as the Trojan Horse Method can be combined with ANC determinations to fix absolute astrophysical cross sections inferred from those peripheral measurements [d36408s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are the limits and specific approximations when computing ANCs and resonance widths with single-channel local potential models? Discuss assumptions about channel coupling, spectroscopic factor = 1, choice of potential geometry and radius, neglect of nonlocality and core excitations, and how these approximations quantitatively affect ANC and Γ predictions.
sub_answers.text:
Single-channel local potential models assume a single open channel and effectively set the many-body spectroscopic strength into a single-particle overlap, which corresponds operationally to taking the spectroscopic factor as unity or absorbing it into the chosen potential [d57152s0p0].
Those models neglect channel coupling, nonlocality, and explicit core excitations, and they therefore miss three-body Coulomb dynamics and exchange effects that can make transfer amplitudes and ANCs model-dependent [d57152s0p0].
Such omissions can produce large uncertainties in predicted ANCs and resonance widths and can yield large error bars in extracted values from fits, as seen in analyses of alpha+core systems where imposed conditions change ANC results and error estimates substantially [d69413s0p0].
Resonance width values are also sensitive to wavefunction non-orthogonality and perturbations of the closed-system states, which can shift widths relative to single-channel predictions [d13548s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do isospin-breaking effects such as Coulomb energy shifts and charge-symmetry-breaking nuclear interactions modify the relation between measured asymptotic normalization coefficients (ANCs) and resonance widths for mirror nucleus pairs?
sub_answers.text: Coulomb interaction and other isospin-symmetry-breaking (ISB) parts of the nuclear interaction break isospin symmetry and modify mirror mass differences relevant to relating ANCs and resonance widths [d83088s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What quantitative biases occur when one assumes a purely peripheral reaction mechanism and a single-particle spectroscopic factor (or independent-particle wave function) in converting ANCs into decay widths, and how do core excitations and multi-configuration admixtures change those predictions?
sub_answers.text: Inelastic coupled-channel rescattering and final-state interactions modify reaction amplitudes and introduce nonzero relative phases that invalidate simple single-particle conversions of ANCs to widths based on independent-particle assumptions [d143284s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In extracting ANCs from transfer or breakup experiments, how sensitive are the resulting values to choices of optical-model potentials, nonlocality corrections, finite-range versus zero-range approximations, and omitted reaction channels, and how do these modeling choices propagate into width uncertainties?
sub_answers.text: Using ANCs from ab initio inputs to fix EFT couplings shows that choices of input data and theoretical constraints affect the extracted parameters and resulting observables, implying modeling choices in reaction analysis propagate into width uncertainties [d28818s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which specific theoretical breakdowns (e.g., failure of Breit–Wigner single-level formalism, energy-dependent penetrability, or significant channel mixing) cause ANC-based width estimates to be unreliable for broad resonances or closely spaced overlapping resonances?
sub_answers.text: Inelastic coupled-channel rescattering and resonance formation in the final state produce nonzero relative phases and channel mixing that break the simple single-level Breit–Wigner picture used in ANC-based width estimates [d143284s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: To what extent does neglecting explicit coupling to other open channels, virtual excitations into the continuum, and nonresonant background contributions bias ANC-derived estimates of partial and total widths, and what observable signatures indicate such omissions are important?
sub_answers.text: Omitting explicit coupling to other open channels and virtual continuum excitations permits inelastic rescattering and resonance formation to alter amplitudes and phases, thereby biasing ANC-derived partial and total width estimates [d143284s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe how asymptotic normalization coefficients (ANCs) are converted into resonance partial widths and then incorporated into thermonuclear reaction rate calculations for stellar nucleosynthesis networks (include formulae and assumptions used in Hauser-Feshbach or narrow-resonance approximations).
sub_answers.text: Resonance parameters are extracted using multichannel, two-body unitary R-matrix methods which produce resonance energies and widths for incorporation into reaction-rate calculations [d18390s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain how experimentally or theoretically determined ANCs constrain cross sections and S-factors for proton-capture reactions on proton-rich nuclei near the drip line (e.g., 17F(p,γ)18Ne, 26Si(p,γ)27P), and how those constraints reduce uncertainties in astrophysical reaction rates.
sub_answers.text: Identification of a specific resonance and its spin-parity can unambiguously establish an l-value for proton capture and thus constrain the resonance contribution to the thermonuclear rate within the Gamow window for nova temperatures [d31520s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: For exotic, short-lived nuclei produced in radioactive beam facilities, how are ANC-based theoretical predictions used to extract resonance parameters (energy, proton width, gamma width) from indirect measurements such as transfer reactions or Coulomb breakup, and how do those predictions shape interpretation of the experimental spectra?
sub_answers.text: Reaction-rate calculations combine contributions from direct, pre-equilibrium, and compound processes using models such as Hauser-Feshbach for the compound component, and these resonance parameters are used as inputs to those frameworks [d123407s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Compare the practical benefits of using ANC-derived widths versus direct experimental determination for very narrow resonances (e.g., reduced sensitivity to target thickness, resonance tail extrapolation, and interference effects); in which scenarios does ANC methodology yield more reliable input for reaction-rate evaluations?
sub_answers.text: Monte Carlo reaction-rate frameworks treat resonance-dominated rates and account for correlations when inputs are normalized to a common reference resonance, and these correlated inputs affect the propagated rate uncertainties [d38139s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Summarize case studies where ANC-derived resonance widths were compared to directly measured widths in mirror nuclei (for example, comparisons between 13N–13C, 17F–17O, or other well-characterized mirror pairs), noting how well ANC predictions reproduced measured values and any systematic deviations observed.
sub_answers.text: Experimentally determined resonance energies from beta decay were used to locate proton-capture resonances in the Gamow window and thereby reduce uncertainty in the reaction rate for 30P(p,gamma)31S by assigning a firm spin and parity to a key resonance [d31520s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide a precise, formal definition of the asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) used in nuclear reaction theory, including its mathematical expression in terms of the tail of the bound-state wavefunction and normalization conventions (e.g., single-particle vs. many-body ANCs).
sub_answers.text:
The asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) is the amplitude of the tail of a bound-state nuclear overlap wave function that controls the long-range, asymptotic form of the bound-state wavefunction [d148282s0p0].
The ANC enters formulas that approximate observables sensitive to the external tail, for example energy shifts in finite oscillator bases via the bound-state momentum and the ANC [d17772s0p0].
ANCs computed for shallow final bound states are used to fix reaction-theory couplings in effective field theory descriptions of radiative capture reactions [d28818s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Define a mirror nucleus and describe the expected isospin and charge-symmetry relations between mirror pairs, including examples (e.g., 17O/17F) and which nuclear properties (energy levels, spectroscopic factors) are typically similar or different.
sub_answers.text:
A mirror nucleus is a member of a pair of nuclei related by exchanging protons and neutrons so that they are isospin analogues of each other [d28818s0p0].
Isospin and charge-symmetry relations imply that mirror pairs often exhibit related structure and reaction behavior that can be used to constrain reaction models and couplings [d54989s0p0].
An example of using mirror relations in practice is the use of the isospin mirror process 7Li(n,γ)8Li when studying 7Be(p,γ)8B in effective field theory applications [d28818s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Give the formal definition of a resonance width in both decay-probability language and scattering-theory language: relate the width Γ to lifetime τ, Breit–Wigner parameterization, and S-matrix pole position (Im(E) or complex energy).
sub_answers.text:
Resonant states are included explicitly in scattering amplitudes and S matrices when analyzing low-energy elastic scattering and reaction data [d69413s0p0].
Scattering phase shifts and S-matrix constructions that include resonant and nonresonant parts are used to extract resonant parameters from data [d69413s0p0].
Connections between bound-state properties and continuum resonances are a central theme in building bridges between bound-state calculations and scattering and reaction theory [d54989s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain the theoretical relationship that connects ANCs for bound states in one nucleus to the partial decay widths or resonance parameters of its mirror state, specifying the approximations (e.g., single-particle, Coulomb effects, isospin symmetry) and key formulae used to convert between ANC and width.
sub_answers.text:
The ANC of a bound state is related theoretically to reaction observables such as radiative capture S-factors and to energy shifts in finite bases, and those relations are used to infer resonance or capture strengths using mirror or related processes under isospin symmetry assumptions [d148282s0p0][d17772s0p0][d28818s0p0].
Practically, ANCs computed for a bound final state are used to fix EFT couplings that then determine capture cross sections and resonance behavior in the mirror channel under approximations like single-particle dominance, Coulomb corrections, and isospin symmetry [d28818s0p0][d17772s0p0].
Theoretical analyses of peripheral transfer reactions and pole amplitudes emphasize correct treatment of three-body Coulomb dynamics when extracting ANCs and relating them to widths or astrophysical quantities [d57152s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List the specific experimental quantities that are reported as ANCs in nuclear data sets and papers (for example, reduced widths, single-particle ANC, spectroscopic factors, asymptotic amplitude with units and normalization), and note which are directly measured versus derived.
sub_answers.text:
Published and reported experimental quantities related to ANCs include extracted asymptotic normalization coefficients themselves and asymptotic amplitudes for bound-state tails used in capture calculations [d69413s0p0][d28818s0p0].
Related reported quantities include spectroscopic information used to constrain models and capture S-factors that are then combined with ANCs to determine astrophysical reaction rates [d36408s0p0][d28818s0p0].
ANCs are reported both as values computed from ab initio or transfer-reaction analyses and as inputs used to fix theory couplings or to derive S-factors and recommended reaction rates for astrophysical applications [d28818s0p0][d36408s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What is the explicit single-particle mathematical relation connecting the asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) C, the spectroscopic factor S, and the amplitude (or normalization constant) of the single-particle bound-state wave function b_sp or φ_sp(r) at large r (e.g., C = √S · b_sp), and under which normalization conventions and definitions of overlap functions does that relation hold?

Within the R-matrix framework, how are resonance partial widths Γ_c written in terms of reduced width amplitudes (γ_c or γλc), the chosen channel radius a, and penetration and shift functions (P_l(a), S_l(a)), including the formula Γ_c = 2P_l(a)γ_c^2 and the assumptions behind that expression?

How do Coulomb-modified asymptotic wave functions (e.g., Whittaker functions with Coulomb parameter η and Coulomb phase shifts) enter the procedure that converts a measured proton ANC for a bound mirror state into an estimate of the corresponding neutron resonance property (e.g., resonance energy or width), and what role do binding-energy differences and Coulomb barrier penetration factors play in that mirror-mapping?

What experimental and reaction-theory steps are used to extract ANCs from peripheral transfer reactions such as (d,p) or (3He,d)—for example, choice of beam energy and angles to ensure peripheral dominance, use of DWBA/ADWA or finite-range calculations, normalization of calculated single-particle cross sections to data to obtain C^2, and estimates of systematic uncertainties from optical potentials and non-peripheral contributions?
sub_answers.text: The S-matrix parameters were fitted to phase-shift data by imposing conditions at very low energies to enable calculation of the ANC of the sub-threshold state [d69413s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What specific approximations and model choices enter single-channel potential-model calculations of ANCs and widths—such as the omission of channel coupling and core excitations, use of local Woods–Saxon geometry and fixed radius/ diffuseness, assumption of pure single-particle spectroscopic strength, neglect of nonlocality and energy dependence, and how do these approximations typically affect the computed ANC and width?
sub_answers.text: Gamow single-particle resonant states, bound states, and scattering states of complex energy form a complete Berggren set used to expand weakly bound and resonant nuclear wave functions [d2984s0p0]. The BCS approximation has been used where both upper and lower components of a quasiparticle wave function are assumed to possess the same radial dependence as an associated Gamow state [d2984s0p0].
